brief: near-silence broken by the tick of cooling stone; then the salt-storm roar

denies.why: nothing lives here to make one. Stone Wastes is tier 5 and its silence is the S9 lethality warning (§Seam 3).
no birds in the Stone Wastes, day or night.
RI-WLD10 §7: one of the two regions with no standing water at all.

L1.text: near-silence — the quietest L1 in the game, −34 LUFS-S

layers.L2_null_reason: RI-AUD03 R1: a layer may be declared null and null is a design statement. The Stone Wastes have no moving texture at all — no wind band, no water, no insect mass. The salt-storm is an L3 EVENT, weather-gated, not a continuous mid layer. A texture here would be the additive reflex R1 exists to stop.

L3.text: tick of cooling stone, then the salt-storm roar — the loudest ambience event in the game, weather-gated

L4.text: the last dying Hist — a FAILING version of the Stone Forest's choral hum. The two must be recognisably the same instrument, one of them broken (R6). The Hist's decline stated in sound before it is stated in any book.

derived_from.broken_by: same four partials, detuned 47 cents apart and amplitude-collapsing mid-note; the chord no longer holds.

layers.L4_note: L4 is a DRONE grain: the dying Hist sustains rather than calls. Its interval band is still checked against §A L4 (45–180 s).

provenance: brief and layer intent quoted from corpus/87-audio/RI-AUD03-regional-ambience.md §B, which quotes game/data/world/regions.json. Synth parameters constructed by W1-22: this build has no audio assets and the bed is synthesised, so a synth spec IS the asset.
bed_gain_db_note: Master trim, in dB, that lands this bed on its own bed_lufs_target. Calibrated by measurement (tools/analysis/ambience-render.mjs --calibrate), not guessed. Once written it is a regression fence: change a layer gain and the next render shows the bed off target. The run that writes it and re-measures it is self-fulfilling and proves nothing on its own; the value is in every later run.
